Optimal.Notes: A 40 Hz refresh with a locked 40 fps cap gives smooth, judder-free gameplay at visually pleasing settings; FSR from 1024x640 recovers sharpness well on the 1280x800 panel. This is the sweet spot between image quality and battery for most play sessions.

profiles.Summary: Rise of the Tomb Raider runs well on the Steam Deck under Proton, with a platinum ProtonDB rating indicating it is largely stable and playable with minimal issues. The game's GPU demands sit just above the Deck's comfortable range at native resolution, so FSR upscaling and medium-to-low settings are recommended for a smooth experience.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific player reports were found; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements (GTX 650–980 Ti range) mapped against the Deck's approximate GTX 1050 Ti–class GPU. On your first run, check the frame rate in the Siberian wilderness hub area — if it drops below your cap, reduce Shadow Quality first, then consider lowering Level of Detail or enabling FSR.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling to 1280x800 keeps GPU load low enough for the 8 W TDP cap; the 40 Hz refresh rate matches the 30 fps cap cleanly. Drop Shadow Quality to Low if frame dips persist in jungle or snow areas.

KnownIssues: No Deck-specific player reports were found; profiles are estimated from PC requirements and hardware comparisons.
The game is rated 'Playable' (not Verified), so minor input or UI issues may occur.
High settings at native 1280x800 can push the GPU beyond its comfort zone, causing frame drops in dense areas.
VR features and some DLC content (Blood Ties) may have additional performance overhead.

MaxPerformance.Notes: At full TDP and native resolution the Deck can push 50-60 fps in simpler indoor areas but may dip to 40-45 fps in dense outdoor environments; consider dropping Shadow Quality to Medium or enabling FSR if dips are frequent. Battery life will be short at 15 W, so this profile is best for docked or plugged-in play.

Optimal.Notes: 40 Hz refresh with a matching 40 fps cap delivers a smooth, judder-free feel that is noticeably better than 30 fps; FSR at 1024x640 keeps the image sharp enough at this resolution. Textures and LOD are raised to High to showcase the game's excellent environments without overloading the GPU.

profiles.Summary: Rise of the Tomb Raider runs well on the Steam Deck at Platinum ProtonDB tier, with the RDNA 2 GPU sitting comfortably above the game's minimum spec, making 30–40 fps very achievable at medium settings and 60 fps possible with lower settings and upscaling. The game has full controller support and is Steam Deck Verified (Playable), so it should launch and play out of the box with Proton.
profiles.BasisNote: No Steam Deck–specific player reports were found; profiles are estimated by comparing the game's PC minimum GPU (GTX 650 / HD 7770) and recommended GPU (GTX 970–980 Ti) against the Deck's roughly GTX 1050 Ti–class RDNA 2 GPU. On your first run, check frame times in the Syria open-world area and the Siberian hub — those are the most demanding zones — and drop to the Optimal or MaxBattery profile if you see consistent dips below your target.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render at 960x600 with FSR upscaling to keep the GPU well within the 7 W TDP; shadow quality and AO are the biggest power draws and are reduced or disabled. Half-rate shading is left off as it causes visible artifacts in this title's foliage-heavy environments.

KnownIssues: No Deck-specific player reports were found; profiles are estimated from PC requirements and hardware comparison.
The game may default to high/very high settings on first launch — manually lower settings for stable performance.
VR-related menus or prompts may appear in-game but can be dismissed safely.
Shader compilation stutters may occur on first launch; a short warm-up session is recommended.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Running uncapped TDP at full GPU clock targets 60 fps in open traversal areas, though dense combat or cutscene-heavy sequences may dip to the low 50s; the 60 fps cap prevents runaway power draw in lighter scenes. Very High or Ultra shadow and AO settings are not recommended as they push the GPU past what the Deck can sustain at 60 fps.
